principle: A corporate action may normalize a canonical price series only if a source independent of the price provider confirms it as effective, with a ratio and a date that the price series shows. Price alone never repairs (HOLD_FROM_EVENT_DATE). Retail web pages are never a primary source.

sources.what: EDGAR full-text search (efts.sec.gov/LATEST/search-index) for split language in 8-K/6-K (incl. amendments) plus the filing documents from www.sec.gov/Archives (main document and EX-99 press releases); extracted by quant/engines/sec-corporate-actions.js
sources.coverage: SEC registrants (US domestic issuers; foreign private issuers via 6-K), filings from 2001 (full-text search horizon). Not covered: non-reporting OTC issuers, events before 2001, issuers without a linked CIK. Effective coverage in this audit: the captured price universe starts 2015-01-02 and the collector keeps a filing only from 400 days before a listing's first bar, so the queried 2001-2012 windows return search hits but no in-universe filings (observed identically in runs 38889245815 and 38957800888).
sources.pitSuitability: YES: every event carries the filing date of the document that establishes each stage (stageVisibleAt.ANNOUNCED/APPROVED/EFFECTIVE). A stage is used for an as-of date only when filed on or before it.
sources.splitSupport: forward and reverse splits, share consolidations; stock dividends only when worded as a split
sources.effectiveDate: explicit effective date/time and the first split-adjusted trading session when stated (8-K Item 3.03/5.03 typically states both); undated retrospective statements are kept with confidence MEDIUM and need the ticker in the filing and a unique price match
sources.ratio: exact ratio required (1-for-N, N:1, every N shares into one, number words); ranges and maxima are never a ratio
sources.identity: CIK; linked to a listing through the capture's issuer CIK (legacy, UNVERIFIED status recorded) and confirmed per event by price concordance on the stated session, ticker mention recorded
sources.latency: 8-K within four business days of the event, usually before the effective date; 10-Q/10-K up to a quarter later (PIT_REVISION recorded)
sources.licensing: public SEC data, public domain; commercial use permitted; SEC fair-access policy (declared User-Agent, <= 10 requests/s) respected
sources.access: HTTP JSON API (search, 100 hits per page, 10,000 per query window) and document archive; no key
failureModes: text extraction errors (boilerplate, exhibits restating old events, several ratios in one document) -> range/ambiguity rules, provenance hash per sentence
CIK-to-listing confusion (holding company, share classes, reused tickers) -> price concordance required for CONFIRMED
effective date vs first trading session (after-close effectiveness) -> window of 2 sessions before and 3 after the stated session
issuer announces and then abandons a split -> only EFFECTIVE wording confirms
search outages / rate limiting -> retries, counted in collector stats

sources.what: 10-Q/10-K/20-F statements such as 'On March 3, 2020, we effected a 1-for-25 reverse stock split', only for issuers with a held price discontinuity or a >= 10x overnight move (at most two reports per candidate date, eight per issuer)
sources.pitSuitability: YES, visible from the report's filing date; when that is after the event, the PIT history shows a HOLD (or an unadjusted jump) until the filing (resumeFrom)
sources.effectiveDate: often stated; otherwise undated (MEDIUM, unique price match and ticker mention required)
failureModes: candidate-driven selection (price discontinuities) decides which reports are read: absence of evidence is not evidence of absence

sources.what: DEF 14A/PRE 14A/DEF 14C/PRE 14C hits for 'reverse stock split' (metadata only)
sources.splitSupport: proposals only (ANNOUNCED); never confirms an event
failureModes: most proposals give a range; many are never effected

sources.what: dei/us-gaap shares outstanding already in the canonical capture (fundamentals.shares_outstanding with availableAt)
sources.splitSupport: indirect: a k-fold change of the share count supports or contradicts a price-only split signature; never confirms alone (issuance and buybacks move it too)
failureModes: dilution in distressed issuers mimics a forward split; stale cover-page values

sources.coverage: sparse (51 filers tagged it for CY2023)
sources.reason: ratio without an event date; adds little over the text of the same 10-Q/10-K

sources.what: issuer press releases are used only as filed with the SEC (EX-99 to 8-K/6-K); issuer web sites are not crawled
sources.reason: web pages are not point-in-time, can change after the fact and are not machine-readable at scale

sources.what: api.finra.org otcMarket/otcDailyList: daily corporate-action records with reverseSplitRate/forwardSplitRate, exDate, old/new symbol, dailyListDatetime
sources.coverage: OTC equity securities (FINRA-quoted); history in the public dataset observed from 2018
sources.licensing: FINRA data terms for API datasets need review before redistribution or commercial use; not integrated until reviewed
sources.access: public GET reachable; filtered queries need the documented POST interface (credentialed for some datasets)
sources.reason: licence review open; would close the OTC gap of the SEC source (non-reporting issuers)

sources.what: Nasdaq Daily List, NYSE corporate-action notices
sources.reason: subscription/redistribution terms; no free historical bulk archive (Nasdaq Daily List archive not publicly reachable)

sources.what: provider splitFactor per bar and adjustedClose (cross-check) - the existing canonical input
sources.independence: NOT independent of the price series (same vendor); it is the field whose gaps caused V4-D1
failureModes: undeclared reverse splits with adjustedClose moving with the raw price (V4-D1)

sources.reason: same vendor as the price series (not independent); requires a token not available to this research run
